I waved to you, the sleep still crusting my eyes and dressed in the pajamas I had worn the night before all the while standing in the little foyer of our condo.

I yawn as I stand there, my bare feet on the cool granite sending chills up my spine. You tell me that I really didn't have to get up early to see you off to work, but that was something that just wasn't going to happen, you'd made me promise that we wouldn't go out anywhere tonight for your birthday, this was the very least that I could do. A simple night in with only what we had in the pantry was what I had promised you.

Once I heard the door click behind you I let out a sigh. I'd been afraid I was going to crack and tell you what I had planned, but somehow I'd managed to keep it all bottled up inside of me, even as my chest felt ready to explode. Most days I'd still be asleep for another hour before finally dragging by lazy body out of bed and getting ready for work, but today wasn't like most days. Today, even if you had spent seemingly countless words convincing me that to you it was that. The only problem was that to me it was still special.

After a minute or two of standing there just watching the door, almost to make sure you don't suddenly come back, almost wishing that you would, I turn on my heel and head for the shower. I wash up quickly, just long enough to rinse everything off, not long enough for the water to even get warm.

Stepping out into the condo I run my fingers through my hair and pull it all into a tight ponytail. I look over the condo and all the things I need to get done before the day ends. I smile happy that I never told you I was taking the day off, you never would have let me waste one of my vacation days. I set out on the condo cleaning the entire thing. We've never let it get too dirty, but it simply isn't up to my standards. Setting on to it with my awful and eclectic music collecting playing in the back ground. You know the one, it makes you groan whenever I start it, and I pretend not to see the smile on your lips as we bicker about just how bad it really is. You generally take the stance of horrid, while I argue that it should be considered a crime of war.

It's well after noon once I finally finish getting everything clean just the way I like it, and without taking so much as a moment to check any emails I get on to the next part of the plan, pulling open the fridge and taking out the various ingredients that I need for everything. Occasionally I check my list of ingredients to check just what I still need. Once it is all pilled up on the island counter I marvel at just how much there is. You're going to love this dinner. I think to myself confidently. I start with the main course, it'll take forever in the slow cooker, but with the wine sauce I'm sure it will be fantastic.

I work away singing a song to myself after the play list ends and I am left to my own music. Once I'm finally working on the dessert, my face smudged with streaks of flour across the bridge of my nose. I freeze as I hear the jingle of your keys in the door. I glance over at the time. It's later than I thought it was but you're still home early.

Looking down at myself I'm not sure what to do, I'm in a red tube top and khaki short-shorts along with a apron covered in blooming flowers. I don't have time to get changed or even wash my face, and even if I did all the evidence of my day was still spread across the counters, so instead I do the only thing I can do, walk to the door so that when you come in I can surprise you and greet you.
